questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted nature + culture + relevant courses in English

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The bureaucracy of going abroad is way too overwhelming. So many forms and papers to fill out, signatures, deadlines etc. It feels excessive.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Edinburgh's website has a lot of information but is very confusing. They send a lot of emails, but it's hard to get an overview.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A student advisor

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The university was great at answering emails if there was a question or issue

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The housing was not on campus, but they had several options throughout the city.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: catered or non-catered residences. The downside of non-catered residence was that you had to buy ALL kitchen equipment yourself which seems like quite a waste. They clear out the kitchens entirely after each semester

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's old and run-down. Connect with roomies quickly to buy kitchen stuff together

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They did not have waitlists for courses which meant you had to apply for the same courses again and again and again and hope that a spot opened up at the exact time where your next application was next in line. Seems like an absurd and time-consuming system. Other than that it was fine

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student advisor / visiting student office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get the class I wanted the most. But otherwise it was fine

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can't expect to get the courses you might have chosen the university for ...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3rd year BA courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UCPH is better. More analytical and critical discussions. More theory and in-depth analysis.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Fiction and the Gothic, Religion and Ethics in Literature, Comparative Literature in a European and Global Perspective

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Comparative literature because it gave insights into the literatures of different nationalities and cultures

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Trains can be quite expensive. Having to buy everything for the kitchen was also unexpected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cafés are cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had so many societies which was really nice and the best way to make friends

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a choir and a writer's club and loved both

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go hiking!!! see the mountains

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Everyone was super nice. Food is not so great in Scotland though

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Understanding the accent ... and the lacking supermarkets

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warm and helpful attitude of the Scots.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't expect the academic level to be as high as UCPH's. Join societies. See the old and beautiful parts of campus

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are better and more bus connections throughout the country than you might think. Just different companies

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The atmosphere of Edinburgh and the diverse nature of Scotland

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having enough time. Since it's only elective courses, they don't take each other into account. My three exams were right on top of each other, and I had way too much to read throughout the semester because all three of my courses were very heavy.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
